note_tweet.text:
The biggest opportunities right now:

1. build for agents that need to spend money on APIs (x402 is an open payment standard around HTTP 402, live on base and solana mainnet. coinbase already caps its own agent research payments at $5 each and $50 a day, and stripe and cloudflare already help you take the payment. the gap is a human-readable ledger, a payee allowlist, and a daily cap for people who are not on coinbase's stack. official docs say the standard has 0 fees built in, but gas is still paid on-chain.)

2. build for the moment an agent can pay while you are not in the chat (google donated AP2 v0.2 to the FIDO alliance on 28 apr 2026, including "human not present" payments off a pre-authorized mandate. mastercard co-developed verifiable intent, a tamper-proof log of what you actually authorized. openai's chatgpt wallet, rolling out gradually to eligible US pro users in dots, still makes you approve with face ID or a fingerprint today. "over time, we expect" delegation is not shipped. first version: a plain-language mandate, a revoke button, and a receipt, on one protocol and one rail. visa's intelligent commerce connect is still in pilot. don't try to replace visa.)

3. build for the hangover after an agent checkout (openai's own help page says "ready to check out means your approval is complete. it does not confirm that the merchant has placed your order." a pending charge is not a receipt, and checkout can fail after you approved. first version: a checklist that tells you whether you are in approved, merchant confirmed, issuer pending, posted, failed, or unknown, and who to contact next. don't promise to reverse a charge.)

4. build for the merchant who can't tell a paying agent from a scraper (mastercard's 8 oct 2026 story is already about merchants seeing agentic traffic and not knowing who's behind it. ERC-8004 is still a draft identity, reputation, and validation registry. https://t.co/8xnoktuOQk says it is deployed on 16 networks, including ethereum, base, polygon, and arbitrum. the EIP itself says it cannot guarantee advertised capabilities are real or non-malicious. first version: look up a registration file or your own allowlist, then allow, challenge, or deny. not a global trust bureau.)

5. build a scoped, revocable permission slip for a wallet agent (safe spending limits already let a bot spend a capped amount of a token with no extra signatures, but safe's own docs say they do not restrict who the spender sends to. the policy engine, announced 27 oct 2026, is supposed to add recipient allowlists and delayed authority changes, and "will launch in Q4, 2026." that is this quarter, not generally available today. metamask already has delegation and caveats. first version: one token, one cap, one period, an optional payee allowlist, and a one-tap revoke.)

6. build the on-chain undo window as something a family will actually use (the send waits N hours, pings a second device, and can be cancelled until then. zodiac delay and various guards already exist. the product is the notification and the cancel path, not another solidity module. start with safe, one chain. a delay cannot reverse funds after the transaction has already executed.)

7. build the 90% automated, 10% named-human stamp for a research note (clients often don't care if a model did the heavy lifting. they want one person to check the sources, say what the model invented, and sign "I read this. I would / would not act on it, and why." first version is a paid one-person service with a turnaround in days, not a platform. not investment advice, and not a performance claim.)

8. build provenance for a chart, a screenshot, or a research page (C2PA 2.4, dated april 2026, added an AI disclosure assertion and support for embedding credentials in markdown and HTML. crypto charts still mostly travel as raw images. first version: stamp who made it, when, whether a model was used, and the official or explorer URLs behind the numbers, plus a viewer that shows the credential. a credential can be stripped. human-made is not the same as true.)

9. build "trace this viral number back to an official page or a transaction" (paste a claim or a screenshot. the tool searches official docs, company or regulator pages, and explorers, and either returns a cited primary URL or says no primary source found. no trust score, no price target, no invented accuracy rate.)

10. build a local-first transaction explainer that never uploads the history (it runs on your machine, reads a raw transaction or a local database, uses a local model, and stays offline. rotki already does local portfolio and tax-ready reports, and some wallet explainers send data off-device. this is not a tax calculator.)

11. build a pay-once box for agent policies and API keys (a local process that holds the keys, reads a written policy for which APIs, methods, and daily caps are allowed, and writes an append-only log. pay once, or open-source it and sell setup. this is not another AI trading bot, and it does not help if the laptop is already compromised.)

12. build throwaway wallets for one trip, one conference, or one group chat (prepaid, time-limited spend, optional payee allowlist, scheduled sweep back to the main wallet, then disable. start on one chain and one asset, for example USDC. the user runs it. don't become an unlicensed custodian.)

13. build day-2 care for a weekend-shipped crypto mini-app (anyone can ship a tool in a weekend with a coding agent. almost no one wants to keep the RPC keys, webhooks, and dependencies alive for three years. first version: a monthly retainer for uptime checks, dependency bumps, key rotation reminders, one office hour, and a written runbook. alchemy, infura, quicknode, and defender already exist. sell the boredom, not a new platform.)

14. build a one-job tool an agent can pay for (one question, one answer, paid per call in USDC via x402, with sources and a receipt. example jobs: "is this the official docs URL and the canonical contract for this ticker on this chain?" or "does this agentURI resolve to a well-formed ERC-8004 registration file?" ERC-8004 is still draft. you will be copied. the business is reliability and a clean 402 flow, not a moat around the idea. this is not another all-in-one terminal.)

15. build for someone taking the blame (a named reviewer looks at a token allowance, a safe policy, or a "the model said this is fine" contract read, then signs a short opinion: what it actually permits, what they would or would not sign with their own money, and what they did not check. this is not a security audit. trail of bits, openzeppelin, and spearbit already do those.)

16. build for people who miss being told they're wrong (a paid, adversarial review of a token thesis, a product idea, or a research note. 45 minutes plus a one-page dissent: the weakest assumption, what would change the reviewer's mind, and which claims were unsourced. an optional AI brief beforehand, marked as such. not a signal group, not investment advice.)

17. build a public, signed track record, not a new prediction market (a page where a person, or an agent with a published registration, signs a dated claim, names the official source that will resolve it, and later records how it resolved. no stakes, no order book, no betting venue. polymarket and kalshi already exist as other products.)

18. build a cooling-off and hide-the-triggers layer for gamified trading (the FCA's "gaming trading" research, first published 21 nov 2022 and last updated 3 june 2026, describes celebratory confetti, badges, leaderboards, and flashing red/green price lists, and flags a blur with gambling-like behaviour, especially in crypto and CFDs. UK self-exclusion schemes like GAMSTOP cover licensed gambling, not crypto trading venues. first version: an overlay that hides balances and PnL, suppresses "trade now" pings, and can lock the user out for hours or days with a delay they can't click away. you cannot force every exchange to honor it. this is not treatment.)

19. build a second-device liveness check before a large send or a "support" video call (the 2025 IC3 report, in the FBI's 6 apr 2026 release, added an AI section for the first time: 22,364 complaints and $893,346,472 in reported losses, including voice clones and believable videos of public figures or loved ones. a 20 jul 2026 IC3 PSA warns about deepfake video chats with alleged executives or law enforcement. first version: the send waits, a second device has to pass a liveness check, and the family has a written rule that they will never send funds because someone on a video call told them to. this is not a recovery firm, and it never asks for a seed phrase. IC3 recorded 10,516 recovery-scam complaints and $1.4 billion in losses in 2025. that's a warning, not a market to enter.)

20. build an official-payee check before you, or your agent, hits approve (domain, legal name if published, official docs URL, and for x402 the payTo address, checked against official sources and obvious spoofs. wallets already simulate transactions. the gap is the agent-checkout step, where the "merchant" may not look like a familiar site. don't promise complete coverage.)

21. build a no-ticker, no-confetti mode for people who still want to hold (a read-only front end with delayed or hidden prices, muted notifications, no top movers, no badges, and a slightly inconvenient "show the number" gesture. many apps already hide the balance. few hide the rest of the gamification.)

22. build a background agent that only acts inside a written mandate, then sends a receipt (one pre-approved job: pay this invoice, claim this reward, convert this dust. a scheduled run, a receipt, and a cancel window before any non-trivial send. start with something small and reversible. a generic "AI trading bot that runs while you're away" is not this.)

23. build an agent that sits on hold for an exchange or bank ticket, with a human in the loop (draft, track, and bump a support ticket, then hand it back when a human replies. the client still sends the message. no unsupervised login, no scraping a venue. don't promise to unstick a compliance hold.)

24. build a weekly clinic on what actually changed (a paid hour plus a one-page brief that only cites official docs. the agent-payments stack is moving faster than a course catalog. five official links a week, in plain language, and a human Q&A. no tokens to buy at the end.)

25. build the anti-AI premium as a camera-on research call, with no transcript unless asked (a booked 30-45 minutes on one agreed question, obviously a person, unpolished, named. a short plain-text follow-up. price it as time, not as a platform. not a signal group.)

26. build a family briefing and a dead-man's switch that does not collect seed phrases (a lawyer-involved sealed letter: where the accounts are, which devices, which attorney, which logins exist, not the seeds. a periodic "I'm OK" ping and a documented escalation path. you sell the setup and the yearly drill, not custody. casa inheritance and unchained already sell self-custody inheritance products. casa's docs describe a 6-month verification period after a request. this is the opposite of a recovery firm.)

27. build a self-hosted invoice stack a tiny merchant can actually run, and if they want, one that agents can pay (a paid setup of BTCPay server, which the official site calls a self-hosted open-source processor with 0% processor fees, funds going to your connected wallet, invoices, and lightning, plus a bookkeeping export and a support hour. optional add-on: an x402 endpoint for machine customers. BTCPay itself is free. "0% fees" is the processor fee, not on-chain or lightning fees.)

28. build IRL rooms with no phones and no recording, for people who live on-chain (a dinner or a half-day workshop, a cap on the room, a written no-device rule, a paper agenda, no livestream, no "we're raising." sell tickets. repeat in one city. the differentiator is the no-device rule, not coffee.)

29. build a tiny-market care product for one operator class, and stay there (either day-2 care for BTCPay shops, or a policy-template pack and a working session for treasury teams that want to be ready for safe's policy engine: recipient allowlist, spending cap, first-payment delay. safe invited design partners on 27 oct 2026. you are late if you try to be the platform. the Q4 2026 launch clock will go stale quickly.)

30. build a small-seller kit so a normal site can accept an agent without locking it out (openai's 13 nov announcement says websites need to make sure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and it is publishing a commerce partner playbook, including CDN config for signed requests with web bot auth. first version: one vendor path, a log that separates agent checkout from human checkout, official catalog fields, and a receipt the merchant can match to a dispute. get one shop live and not accidentally blocking a real buyer. you're not becoming visa.)

KEEP BUILDING
